top_choice_rationale: P001 pairs two achievements that each rest on one nameable chemical principle with a quantitative record: reversible-terminator sequencing by synthesis (Balasubramanian, Klenerman), which made reading DNA a scalable measurement, and base editing (Liu), the programmable deamination of one base without a double-strand break, separable from the 2020 cleavage prize by a citation naming the base conversion. Both are mature or well reproduced, the scope of each citation is explicit, and three laureates keep attribution defensible. P004 shares the base-editing part and ranks next; the three-name base-editing prize P002 follows because the TadA argument for Komor and Gaudelli is serious.
